epigraph: The seam feeds the feet that do not stop.
vignette: The ground cracked open near the seam. Raw light poured out. It burned the eyes. The Walker stepped into the gap. He did not flinch. The light touched his skin. It did not burn. It fed him. He walked forward. The stone beneath him turned to glass. He left no footprints. Only light remained. A Verdant scout watched. He raised his spear. He cast a thicket. The vines grew fast. They caught the Walker. The Walker smiled. The Rift breathed. The vines withered. They turned to dust. The dust blew away. The Walker kept walking. He walked over the dead vines. He walked toward the palace-tree. The ground believed in him. The thicket forgot its name. It was unwritten. The Walker was the only truth left. He drank the light. He grew strong. The scout fell back. The ground was empty. Only the Walker remained. He was the seam made flesh. He walked on. The light followed him. It filled his lungs. He did not breathe air. He breathed the wound. He was alive. He was true.
codex_note: The Walker draws sustenance from the wound rather than the world, making him a hazard to those who rely on stable ground.
